title: Coherence of the specified completion-inverse scalar comparisons
statement:
Fix a finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $T$ be a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme with $\ell$ invertible, in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization]; such schemes are called allowed. For each finite $E\subset\Omega$ over $\mathbf Q_\ell$, use the framework integral category and raw rationalization $\mathcal C_E^s(T)$ of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and the PBC integral category and raw rationalization $\mathcal C_E^p(T)$ of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category].
Suppose $I_{T,E}$ and $J_{T,E}$ are the exact integral identity and its raw rationalization, with $J_{T,E}(u\otimes x)=u\otimes x$. Write $S_{L/E}$ for the framework scalar extension [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] with associator $a^s$ [lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition], and $P_{L/E}$ for PBC scalar extension with associator $a^p$ [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. Use the framework associator normalized by conjugating ordinary tensor associativity by the quotient completion maps, as in [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. For every $E\subseteq L$, the specified map $\chi_{L/E}$ [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] restricts to an integral natural isomorphism from ordinary PBC coefficient extension to framework strict-tower extension, after the identity identifications $I$. Its ordinary tensor transport is fixed on tensor generators, its completion chain has the actual quotient-map coordinates and zero shifted-product coordinate, and its localization is the specified integral scalar lift of [def-fd-coefficient-comparison-datum].
Its inverse rationalizes to an exact natural isomorphism
$$j_{T,L/E}:J_{T,L}S_{L/E}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{L/E}J_{T,E}.$$
These comparisons commute with the specified shift maps, have the normalized identity-extension value, and for $E\subseteq L\subseteq M$ satisfy
$$a^p_{M,L,E}\circ P_{M/L}(j_{T,L/E})\circ j_{T,M/L,S_{L/E}K}=j_{T,M/E}\circ J_{T,M}(a^s_{M,L,E}).$$
They satisfy the unit equations and the four-field associativity compatibility for the specified scalar associators, including repeated fields.

proof.text: Use the integral identity identifications in the hypothesis throughout. Write $C_{L/E}(K)=K\otimes^L_{R_E}R_L$ for ordinary extension and $U_{L/E}$ for framework strict-tower extension. The stratified-perfect characterization identifies both integral categories as the same full subcategory of $D(R_E)$. Finite-free constructible scalar transport puts $C_{L/E}K$ in the common category over $L$. Every such $K$ is derived complete, so the finite-free completed comparison supplies a natural isomorphism $b_{L/E,K}=\chi_{L/E,K}:C_{L/E}K\to U_{L/E}K$. Its target is in the same full category because it is isomorphic to $C_{L/E}K$. Thus $b$ and its inverse restrict to the integral categories; their naturality is the ambient derived naturality, not just naturality on chain maps.

proof.text: Retain the specified map, rather than choose an isomorphism between its source and target. For a flat-term K-flat representative $P$, its $m$th quotient coordinate sends $p\otimes s$ to $p\otimes\bar s$ and its shifted-product coordinate is zero. Ordinary change of coefficient presentation sends each tensor generator to that same generator under the identity ring identifications. Hence its transport is the prescribed ordinary tensor transport, and the comparison with derived localization is exactly the quotient-completion map with the canonical resolving comparisons. The descent lemma applies with $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,T}$, $S=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,T}$ and $B_n=(\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^n)_T$: these are commutative $S$-algebras with $S$-linear transitions, and countable products of $S$-module sheaves on the pro-etale site are exact by the countable-products lemma. It makes this equation independent of $P$. This verifies the integral-lift normalization requested by the definition of comparison datum; no existence assertion is being taken from that definition.

proof.text: Ordinary derived change of rings is exact. The common integral category has the inherited distinguished triangles, so its restriction $C_{L/E}$ is exact. The completed-scalar shift lemma gives $\sigma^U_{m,K}b_{K[m]}=b_K[m]\sigma^C_{m,K}$ for every integer $m$ with the specified shifts. In its reordered cone the comparison is $(x,y)\mapsto(x,(-1)^m y)$; applying it to $(c(z),0)$ gives $(c(z),0)$, which is why no sign appears in the completion map itself. Consequently $\sigma^C_{m,K}b_{K[m]}^{-1}=b_K^{-1}[m]\sigma^U_{m,K}$. A triangle and its image under $U$ are identified by $b$ with its distinguished image under $C$, including the last arrow by this shift equation. Thus $U$ is exact with its specified shifts, and $b$ and $b^{-1}$ are exact natural isomorphisms.

proof.text:
Let $A^C_{M,L,E}:C_{M/L}C_{L/E}\to C_{M/E}$ be ordinary tensor associativity and $A^U$ the specified integral framework associator. The scalar-completion associator lemma gives
$$A^U_K\,U_{M/L}(b_{L/E,K})\,b_{M/L,C_{L/E}K}=b_{M/E,K}\,A^C_K.$$
Its maps use the actual quotient cocones and are resolution independent. The normalization in the hypothesis, as specified in the integral realization node, identifies this $A^U$ with the framework associator used here: it is the conjugate of this same $A^C$ by these same maps $b$. Thus the displayed equality holds for the chosen associator, not merely for some associator. Ordinary tensor transport in step 2 identifies $A^C$ with the integral balancing whose rationalization is the specified PBC associator.

source.place: Final coefficient-category sentence; expanded completion-inverse scalar comparison from lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison, old proof steps 3–4 (agent argument).

proof.text:
Naturality of $b_{M/L}$ at $b_{L/E,K}$ rewrites the middle factors in step 4 as
$$U_{M/L}(b_{L/E,K})\,b_{M/L,C_{L/E}K}=b_{M/L,U_{L/E}K}\,C_{M/L}(b_{L/E,K}).$$
Insert this equality in step 4, multiply on the left by $b_{M/E,K}^{-1}$, and on the right by $C_{M/L}(b_{L/E,K}^{-1})\,b_{M/L,U_{L/E}K}^{-1}$. The result is precisely
$$A^C_K\,C_{M/L}(b_{L/E,K}^{-1})\,b_{M/L,U_{L/E}K}^{-1}=b_{M/E,K}^{-1}\,A^U_K.$$
Here functoriality sends $b^{-1}$ to the inverse of the image of $b$; all adjacent pairs cancel. This is the integral inverse-comparison cocycle, with the direction of every arrow fixed.

proof.text: For $L=E$, multiplication identifies $C_{E/E}$ with the identity, and the finite-free completed comparison identifies $b_{E/E}$ with the natural completeness unit $K\to U_{E/E}K$. Thus $b_{E/E}^{-1}$ is exactly the normalized unit $U_{E/E}\to\mathrm{id}$. The scalar-completion associator lemma supplies the unit equations with these multiplication/completeness identifications. Setting $L=E$ or $M=L$ in step 5 therefore gives the two unit comparison squares; with all fields equal it gives the identity square. This also covers a repeated field adjacent to a strict extension: no strict-inclusion hypothesis was used in steps 1–5.

source.place: Final coefficient-category sentence; expanded completion-inverse scalar comparison from lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison, old proof steps 3–4 (agent argument).

proof.text: Localize $b^{-1}$ over the final field, defining $j_{T,L/E}=Q_L(b_{L/E}^{-1})$. The raw rationalizations have the same objects and tensor-localized Hom groups. Their identity equivalences send each integral map and each scalar to itself, so the source is exactly $J_{T,L}S_{L/E}$ and the target is $P_{L/E}J_{T,E}$. Semilinear localization applies: the image of $\varpi_E$ is nonzero in $L=\mathcal O_L[1/\varpi_L]$, hence invertible. Both scalar functors are semilinear by coefficient multiplication on tensors; the comparison components are $R_L$-linear. The localization lemma preserves exact transformations, inverses, composition and whiskering. It therefore sends the inverse equation of step 5 to the displayed $a^p\,P(j)\,j=j\,J(a^s)$, and preserves the shift and unit equations. In particular the integral lift retained in step 2 is still the specified lift, not a newly chosen map.

proof.text:
Finally take $E_0\subseteq E_1\subseteq E_2\subseteq E_3$ and abbreviate $S_{ba}=S_{E_b/E_a}$, $P_{ba}=P_{E_b/E_a}$, $J_b=J_{T,E_b}$ and $j_{ba}=j_{T,E_b/E_a}$. Suppressing component subscripts, the comparison from $J_3S_{32}S_{21}S_{10}$ to $P_{32}P_{21}P_{10}J_0$ is
$$D=(P_{32}P_{21}j_{10})(P_{32}j_{21}S_{10})(j_{32}S_{21}S_{10}).$$
Twice applying the cocycle of step 7, and moving the inner $j$ past an associator by naturality, identifies the two contractions of $D$ with
$$j_{30}J_3\bigl(a^s_{3,2,0}\,S_{32}(a^s_{2,1,0})\bigr),\qquad
j_{30}J_3\bigl(a^s_{3,1,0}\,(a^s_{3,2,1}S_{10})\bigr).$$
The scalar-completion associator law makes these equal, and localization preserves that law. The PBC associators have the corresponding coherence by their scalar-extension proposition. These are exactly the four-field compatibility diagram for the specified comparisons. The same substitutions with units give its degeneracies, since step 6 included equal fields. All manipulations here are substitution, naturality and cancellation of already supplied natural isomorphisms.
